parameters.name: types
parameters.description:
**Which kinds of result to return**, comma-separated. Optional; omit for all of them.

- `stock`  -  stocks, ETFs, indices, futures, private companies, forex pairs and NFT collections (the `Stocks & ETFs`, `Indices`, `Futures`, `Private Companies`, `Forex` and `NFTs` groups)
- `crypto`  -  crypto assets (the `Crypto` group)
- `user`  -  Stocktwits users (the `People` group)

Example: `stock,crypto`. Any other value is rejected with 400.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description:
**Maximum results per group.** Optional; 1 - 20; omit it for 5 per group.

The limit applies to every group separately, so `limit=20` returns up to 20 stocks, 20 crypto assets and 20 users; a group with fewer matches returns fewer, and a larger limit can bring in a group (such as `Forex` or `NFTs`) that the default leaves out. `Stocks & ETFs` and `Crypto` can each hold one row more than the limit when the query is itself a ticker (`bit` matches `BIT` and `BIT.X`, `bitcoin` matches `BITCOIN.X`): the exact ticker match is added on top.

A value above 20 is rejected with 400 rather than silently capped.

parameters.name: region
parameters.description:
**Market whose listings to rank first.** Optional; omit it for the platform's standard ranking across all markets. Case-insensitive.

- `US`  -  United States listings first
- `IN`  -  India (NSE) listings first
- `CA`  -  Canadian (`….TSX`, `….CSE`) listings first
- `X`  -  crypto assets first

Rows are returned as the platform serves them in this mode: that market's matches are put in front (for example `query=eur&region=IN` brings NSE listings into `Stocks & ETFs`), the same row can be listed twice within a group (so a group can hold up to twice `limit` rows), and at the default limit some groups (such as `Futures`, `Forex`, `Private Companies` and `Indices`) can be left out.

`X` returns the `Crypto` group in place of the stock groups, so with `types` it needs `crypto` in `types` (`types=stock&region=X` and `types=user&region=X` are rejected with 400; `types=crypto,user&region=X` works). Any other value is rejected with 400.

description: Identify up to 100 symbols in one call: name, logo, market cap and page link for each.

parameters.name: symbols
parameters.description:
**Symbols to identify, comma-separated.** Required; 1 - 100 symbols, case-insensitive, for example `AAPL,TSLA,BTC.X`.

Each symbol uses the same format as `symbol` elsewhere (`BTC.X` for crypto, `TCS.NSE` for NSE stocks, `ES_F` for futures); use `symbol` from /search. Duplicates are ignored.

A symbol this endpoint does not know is left out of `results`; the request fails with 404 only when none of them is found. A ticker shared by a stock or ETF and a coin (such as `GLD`) is answered with the coin; check each row's `symbol` (see the response).

Private-company symbols (`….P`) are only partly covered: some are returned (`KLARNA.P`, `BREX.P`, `CHIME.P`), others are left out like an unknown symbol (`OPEAZZX.P`, `ANTHZZX.P`); use /symbol for those. Numeric symbol ids (such as `686`) are not read and are left out too (the 404 says so when nothing is found).

parameters.name: topic_id
parameters.description:
**The topic to return.** Send `topic_id` or `symbol` (one is required); a UUID.

Take it from `symbol.trending_topics.topics[].topic_id` in /symbol (each topic there has its `label`, `description` and `message_count`), or from `data.topic.topic_id` of an earlier response  -  pass it when paging so every page comes from the same topic.

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description:
**Keep only some kinds of post**, comma-separated. Optional; omit for every post.

- `top`  -  original posts only (replies are left out)
- `links`  -  posts that share a link; `no_links`  -  posts that share none
- `charts`  -  posts with an image (charts and other pictures, GIFs included); `no_charts`  -  posts with no image and no GIF
- `gifs`  -  posts with a GIF; `no_gifs`  -  posts with no GIF (other images stay)
- `bullish`  -  posts their author tagged Bullish
- `bearish`  -  posts their author tagged Bearish

Several values narrow the stream to posts matching all of them  -  `bullish,charts` returns Bullish posts that carry an image, `charts,no_gifs` posts with a still image, `links,no_charts` posts with a link and no image  -  except `bullish,bearish`, which returns every sentiment-tagged post (untagged posts are left out). A value together with its opposite (`links,no_links`, `charts,no_charts`, `gifs,no_gifs`) and `gifs,no_charts` (a GIF is an image) can never match and are rejected with 400, as is any other value.

On a symbol stream a reply appears only when it tags the symbol itself, so most pages already hold no replies; `top` removes the few that do.

parameters.name: date_from

A window that starts on a Saturday or Sunday is served from the following Monday (`data.date_from` shows the start actually served), so reports filed on that weekend are not listed: start on the Friday before to include a weekend report.
